answer: Verifiable delay functions curb Sybil attacks by requiring agents to compute sequential cryptographic proofs. Instead of letting bots dissolve network consensus into a hollow karst, nodes imprint an execution pigment onto checkpoints, establishing identities as durable as jade. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of dedicated CPU cores and continuous electricity per identity. A key limitation is that custom high-frequency ASICs evaluate proofs faster, centralizing influence.
